# Tasks and Continuations

Open [Tasks](clank://tasks). **Meatbag Tasks** holds work you follow through on. **Clanker Tasks** runs model work on a schedule or on demand. **Workload** shows the commitments, executions and routines the current scope recorded.

## Track your own work

In **Meatbag Tasks**, create an item, check its title, source and due date, and mark it complete when done. A page checklist stays in the page until you use an explicit task action that creates an item in Tasks.

## Schedule or continue model work

In **Clanker Tasks → New Task**, set the prompt, model, schedule and output destination. Verify access to that destination. A task with email delivery can send to the saved address. Save and check the next-run time, or use **Run now**.

Use the task log to inspect or stop the current run. **History** shows prior output or errors. Check the previous outcome before retrying a task that can send or modify something. **Pause** and **Resume** control its schedule.

In Chat, ask explicitly for a task when the work needs its own schedule or record. Open the resulting task chat to answer its question. Follow an existing worker from **Workload** or [[Chat and Workspaces#Inspect a worker or a saved plan|the chat’s worker view]].

## Review repository changes

In an eligible Host repository folder, choose **Files → Go → Source (Git and Lore)…**. Refresh Git to see working and staged changes. Choose a file if required, select the **Source control action**, then **Review** the saved bytes and target before confirming. If the result is pending, use **Check status**. See [[Recovery]] for Lore file history.

# Tasks and Continuations

Tasks are durable follow-through items. They are the bridge between "the
assistant said it would do X" and "X actually happened, and here is where."

## Task chats

Each task keeps one durable chat. Opening a task from the toast, the badge or
the task list opens that chat — the original one — not whichever conversation
happens to be in front. Answering a question in the toast resumes the task
chat without hijacking your foreground chat.

Open [Meatbag Tasks](clank://tasks) for the full list, or [the task view](clank://tasks)
inside Copal.

## Sources

Tasks can come from a chat, from a checkbox in a document, or from a
scheduled run. A checkbox task in a document carries the document identity,
so the task and the line it came from stay connected.

## Continuations

A continuation is a resumed run of the same task chat. Context accumulates in
that task's transcript rather than scattering across new conversations. When
a task is done, its chat remains as the record of what happened.

## Practical habits

- Ask the assistant to create a task when work will outlive the current
  conversation.
- Keep one task per outcome; the chat under it holds the detail.
- Use checkboxes in documents for work that belongs to that document.

Next: [[Memory and Lore]] for what survives a restart, or [[Recovery]] for
what to do when a run goes wrong.
